newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Alcohol makers favour advertising self-regulation.
newsitem.headline: Alcohol makers favour advertising self-regulation.

text.p: The regulation of advertising for alcoholic beverages is accomplished faster and more cheaply when left in the hands of the industry than when turned over to governments, an official with a Western European alcohol trade group told an advertising conference here on Wednesday.

"We believe that self-regulation has many advantages over a purely regulatory approach," Richard Owen, chairman of the Amsterdam Group Working Committee, told the "West Goes East" conference on self-regulation.
"Experience shows that it is usually quicker, more flexible and cheaper for the consumer," Owen said.

The Amsterdam Group, an association of 15 companies that produce and market alcoholic beverages in Europe, aims to strengthen political and social acceptance that alcoholic beverages are consumer products and compatible with healthy lifestyles, recognise the existence of misuse and act to combat the misuse, and recognise that there can be both favourable and unfavourable health implications from alcohol consumption.
Owen said governments can play a valuable role in regulating the advertisement of alcohol.
"Indeed, the ideal consumption appears to be a minimum framework legislative regime, within which self-regulation can operate speedily and effectively," Owen said.
But a purely legislative approach can be rigid and time- consuming to enforce, he said.
"But self-regulation is not, or must not be, a soft option or merely a public relations exercise," he said, emphasising that a successful system takes considerable time to both set up and administer.
